checks.claim: PB0: K0=2^a/(1-a) and the vector Schur bound (20) define a bounded map J_G:L2(I;G)->H_t tensor G with the stated bilinear identity.
checks.reason: The row integral [s^(1-a)+(1-s)^(1-a)]/(1-a) is concave and symmetric, with maximum 2^a/(1-a) at s=1/2. Cauchy-Schwarz against K(s,t)dt gives ||KF||2<=K0||F||2. Inner-product Cauchy-Schwarz then gives (20) on simple fields. Scalar L2 enters H_t by the same bound on smooth differences, so the inclusion is well defined. Simple-field density extends the map, and the bilinear integral is continuous by Schur, so the identity extends. No raw multiplier or Hilbert-valued Gaussian occurs.

checks.claim: PB0: (C_t tensor Id)J_G F equals the temporal Bochner convolution a.e. and lies in Lr(I;G).
checks.reason: The Bochner version is bounded L2->L2 with norm <=K0. On tensors of smooth time and G elements it is the definition of C_t. The approximants converge in L2 by Schur, and the composed map converges in Lr by U(15) with (20), since r>=2. Lr embeds in L2 on the unit interval, so uniqueness of L2 limits gives a.e. equality and Lr membership. No additional convolution theorem is used.

checks.claim: PB0: bound (21), nonseparable membership and raw cost (22) hold for all H:homog Gamma, including white and singular measures.
checks.reason: In the absolute integral only x in B and y in B-B contribute, so the bound |B|Gamma(B-B)||q||inf^2 holds. B-B is compact and Gamma is Radon and positive, so the constant is finite, including white and invariant-direction singular measures. Uniform continuity of Psi and (21) give continuity of t->Psi_t in H_sp. Hence Psi lies in L2(I;H_sp). Tonelli/Fubini with the finite bound identifies ||Psi||^2 with int Psi h_Psi=v_Psi, which is the UL cost.

checks.claim: PB0: mean identity (23), including the explicit canonical all-s, all-R version.
checks.reason: With z=(f,0), w=(0,Lambda g), U(2) gives <q,m_R f g>_H_sp. Fubini with q the temporal integral gives int m_R h_s f g. Both sides are bounded E operators of the form (0,Mu). Smooth displacements are dense in Hhalf and Lambda(smooth) is dense in Hminus-half, so equality extends to E. At fixed smooth Psi the H_sp integral exists at every s with norm <=K0 sup||Psi_t||. The explicit operator therefore agrees a.e. with the completed mean class and has the same rate integral. No simultaneous representative over rough controls is claimed.

checks.claim: PB1: membership of normalized labels and exact row identity (24), with one m=eta^2, one Gamma and no Fourier factor, extended to all signed raw Phi.
checks.reason: h_i is in L2 and hence in H_t, and the compact smooth products are H_sp tests. The row product is (eta_R f)(eta_R Lambda^-1 Lambda f)=m_R f^2. Under the unitary Fourier convention the H-1/2 metric cancels Lambda, so the row equals the L2 pairing with no c_d factor. The H_sp pairing contains Gamma once. Time pairing gives <h,h_i>=(1/ell)int_Ii C_t h. Both sides are bounded on H_I: the right by ell^(-1/r)C_mean||Phi||||f||Hhalf^2, by Holder and U(17). Dense tensors therefore extend the identity to all of H_I.

checks.claim: PB1: entrywise order (25), PSD of each Gram, and every PG guard, without a Loewner assumption.
checks.reason: Each entry factors as a nonnegative time pairing times a physical spatial pairing. K, Gamma, f^2 and h_i are nonnegative and 0<=m_R<=1, so 0<=C_R<=D entrywise by Tonelli. Each matrix is a Gram matrix and hence PSD; no order of the difference is used. H_I is real Hilbert, ell_i>0, b_i>=0, and ell,b are common to both matrices. Vanishing masked labels are covered by PG Section7 eligibility. PG is used only on optimized scores.

checks.reason: For the family-dependent R', k_i^R'=k_i^inf. Then (24) and the Rayleigh formula give sqrt((<Phi,k_i>-b_i)_+)<=lambda(avg). Next lambda<=max(1,||L||)<=1+||L||, Bochner contraction, sum ell_i=1 and L1<=Lr give 2+2Cq-q^2/2. For q>4C+4 this is <2-2q<0. checks.reason: With B=1, delta=1/n, n>=2, US gives N=n, ell_N=0, and the error e_n is uniform in R>=1 on the M-ball. Density of normalized real compact trials and H1 form continuity give (28). No continuum selector or optimization/limit interchange occurs.
